title: go in, fall off, run away etc. (phrasal verbs 1)
subtitle: go in / get out / stand up / come back
summary: Learn phrasal verbs: a verb like go, look or get plus a word like in, out, up, down, away, back, over or round.

lesson.heading: What is a phrasal verb?
lesson.text: A phrasal verb is a verb (**go**, **look**, **get**, **be** etc.) + **in**, **out**, **up**, **down** etc. **in** = into a place. **out** = out of a place.

examples.text: I waited outside the shop. I didn't **go in**.
Sarah opened the door of the car and **got in**.
I went to the window and **looked out**.
The car stopped and a woman **got out**.

left.label: on
examples: The bus came, and I **got on**.

right.label: off
examples: The bus stopped, and she **got off**.

lesson.heading: up and down
lesson.text: **up** = to a higher place or position. **down** = to a lower place or position.

examples.text: He **stood up** and left the room.
We **looked up** at the stars in the sky.

left.label: away or off (= from a place)
examples: Emma got into the car and **drove away**.
Tim has **gone away** for a few days.

right.label: back (= to the place again)
examples: We went out for dinner and then **went back** to our hotel.
Tim is away. He'll **be back** on Monday.

lesson.heading: over and round (or around)
lesson.text: **over** = from one side to the other side, or to the other side of a page. **round** (or **around**) = in a circle, so that you face the other way.

examples.text: The wall wasn't very high, so we **climbed over**.
**Turn over** and look at the next page.
Somebody shouted my name, so I **looked round**.
We went for a long walk. After an hour we **turned round** and went back.

lesson.heading: More phrasal verbs
rows: stop working (a car or a machine)

lesson.text: *round* and *around* mean the same in these verbs: *I looked round* = *I looked around*.

exercises.prompt: The door was open, so we went ___.
exercises.explanation: go in = go into a place.

exercises.prompt: He heard a plane, so he looked ___.
exercises.explanation: look up = turn your eyes to a higher place.

exercises.prompt: The bus stopped, and she got ___.
exercises.explanation: We get on a bus and we get off it.

exercises.prompt: There was a free seat, so she sat ___.
A car stopped, and two men got ___.
exercises.explanation: get out = get out of a car.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.
Does the sentence need away or back?

items.text: Wait a minute. Don't go ___. I want to ask you something.
Emma got into the car and drove ___.
Tim has gone ___ for a few days.
Mark lives in London now, but he wants to go ___ to Canada.
We went out for dinner and then went ___ to our hotel.
Tim is away. He'll be ___ on Monday.

exercises.prompt: When you have read this page, turn ___ and read the other side.
exercises.explanation: turn over = turn a page to the other side.

exercises.statement: The train slowed down and finally stopped.

exercises.prompt: I like flying, but I'm always nervous when the plane ___.
The fire alarm ___ and everyone had to leave the building.
exercises.explanation: go off = start ringing. The past of go is went.

exercises.prompt: You are in the street. Somebody behind you shouts your name. Put the sentence in order.
exercises.answer: Somebody shouted my name, so I looked round.
exercises.explanation: look round (or look around) = turn so that you can see behind you.
